summary.question: What is CarSalesTeam?
summary.answer: CarSalesTeam is a managed workflow service for dealer groups and their dealerships that brings vehicle enquiries, test-drive requests and service follow-ups into one workflow, with your sales and service teams in control. Every enquiry gets a clear next step, and staff confirm inventory and appointments before anything is promised.
takeaways: Every enquiry gets a clear next step and a named person to confirm it.
Vehicle availability, discounts, financing, trade-in valuations and repair authorisations stay with authorised staff.
Staff confirm inventory and appointments before anything is promised.
Results are measured by enquiries with a confirmed next step, compared with how you work today.

scope.covers: Vehicle enquiries, test-drive requests and service-visit requests prepared for staff confirmation, for the dealerships and enquiry sources you choose.
scope.excludes: Confirming vehicle availability, discounts, financing, trade-in valuations, fault diagnosis and repair authorisations.
scope.instead: Those stay with the sales manager, the service desk or other authorised staff.

statement: Your team has a dealership to run.
Keep enquiries moving from first contact to a confirmed next step.

workflow.heading: A reply is the beginning.
workflow.intro: One task, start to finish: following up sales and service enquiries, and where your staff decide.
workflow.body: A shopper asks about a vehicle. The answer needs current inventory, a clear owner and a follow-up. The service desk needs the same discipline. Here is every step from the shopper’s enquiry to the closed record, and where your staff decide.

steps.title: The enquiry arrives
steps.body: A shopper asks about a vehicle, a test drive or a service visit through the website form, by phone or by message, on the channels your dealership chose. Every enquiry goes into one shared list.
steps.label: Request in
steps.does: Asks about a vehicle on the website form, by phone or by message. It joins one shared list.

chat.text: Is the white hatchback still in? I'd like to see it this week and trade in my sedan.

steps.title: CarSalesTeam reads it
steps.body: It works out what kind of enquiry it is and how urgent, and picks out the details: the vehicle, the preferred time, the contact details and anything that needs a manager.
steps.label: Sorted
steps.does: Sorts it by type and urgency and picks out the vehicle, the preferred time, the contact details and anything for a manager.

chat.text: Sorted as a vehicle enquiry. Vehicle: white hatchback. Time: this week. Trade-in: sedan.

steps.title: CarSalesTeam checks the context
steps.body: It checks the inventory and scheduling sources you allow and your dealership rules. Earlier enquiries come from your CRM only where that connection is agreed after an assessment.
steps.label: Checked
steps.does: Checks the inventory, scheduling sources and dealership rules you allow, and your CRM only where that is agreed.

chat.text: Checked the stock record: one white hatchback listed. Viewing not yet confirmed.

steps.title: The shopper hears back
steps.approval: Your team approves messages to customers
steps.body: It drafts a reply with the expected response time from your rules. Your team approves messages to customers before they go out.
steps.label: Reply drafted
steps.does: Drafts a reply with the response time from your rules.

chat.text: Thanks, Chris. A sales adviser will confirm the car and a time within 2 hours.
Approved. Send it.

steps.title: The right person gets a full brief
steps.body: Routine enquiries go to a sales adviser or the service desk with everything they need. Discounts, financing, trade-in valuations and repair authorisations go to the sales manager or service manager to decide.
steps.label: Handed off
steps.does: Briefs a sales adviser or the service desk. Discounts, financing, trade-in valuations and repair authorisations go to the sales or service manager.

chat.text: Brief to Nina: white hatchback, this week, Chris's number. Trade-in value to the sales manager.

steps.title: Nothing is left waiting
steps.body: The enquiry stays open against its expected time. If it slips, CarSalesTeam reminds the owner and escalates to the role you name.
steps.label: Chased
steps.does: Keeps the enquiry open against its expected time. If it slips, it reminds the owner, then escalates to the role you name.

chat.text: No confirmation after 1 hour. Reminder sent to Nina.

steps.title: Staff confirm, the loop closes
steps.body: Staff confirm the vehicle, the slot or the visit; a reply alone does not close an enquiry. CarSalesTeam prepares the follow-up to the customer for your team’s approval.
steps.label: Confirmed
steps.approval: Your team approves the follow-up to the customer
steps.does: Staff confirm the vehicle and the slot; a reply alone does not close an enquiry.

chat.text: Car is on site. Booked Thursday 5 pm with me; the sales manager will value the sedan.
You're booked: white hatchback, Thursday 5 pm, with Nina. Bring the sedan for a valuation.

steps.title: Logged and reported
steps.body: The enquiry is logged with who did what and when, and counted in regular reports on response time, enquiries with a confirmed next step, unresolved leads and staff effort.
steps.label: Closed
steps.does: Logs who did what and when, and counts it in regular reports on response time, confirmed next steps, unresolved leads and staff effort.

chat.text: Logged: viewing booked, each approver recorded. Enquiry closed.

demo.heading: From first message to closed and logged.
demo.body: Follow each enquiry end to end: how it arrives, what is checked, who is told, where your team approves, and how it is closed and recorded. Every step names who acts.

scenes.request: My car is due for a service. Do you have a slot next week?
scenes.rule: Use approved service categories and scheduling access. Do not diagnose a fault.

steps.does: Emails the service desk asking for a service slot next week.
steps.short: Request arrives by email.
steps.label: Request in

chat.text: My car is due for a service. Do you have a slot next week?

steps.does: Sorts it as a routine service visit, notes the preferred week and flags the missing details: the vehicle and its mileage.
steps.short: Sorts it as a routine service and flags what is missing.
steps.label: Sorted

chat.text: Sorted as a routine service. Missing: which vehicle, and its mileage.

steps.does: Checks the approved service categories, the scheduling access you allow and any service history it is permitted to read. It does not diagnose a fault.
steps.short: Checks service categories and scheduling access.
steps.label: Checked

chat.text: Checked the service categories: routine service. No fault reported, nothing to diagnose.

steps.does: Drafts a reply that confirms receipt, gives the expected response time and asks for the vehicle and mileage.
steps.short: Drafts a reply and asks for the missing details.

Approved. Send it.

chat.text: Booked Tuesday 8:00, routine service. Any repair needs our sign-off first.

steps.short: Drafts the confirmation; the desk approves it.
steps.approval: The desk approves the confirmation before it is sent.

Approved. Send it.

faq.q: Does this connect to our DMS or CRM?
faq.a: Only if that is agreed after an assessment. We assess your existing systems, permissions and integration options before agreeing scope; no integration with a particular DMS or CRM is promised in advance.

faq.q: Can it quote prices or approve financing?
faq.a: No. It can share approved information within agreed limits, but discounts, financing decisions and trade-in commitments remain with authorised staff.

faq.q: Does it handle both sales and service?
faq.a: Yes, if you agree both. Sales and service each run as their own workflow, with their own approval rules and their own results.
